summary: This section explains how annual reports for certain Government companies must be handled. When the Central Government is a member, it must prepare an annual report and present it in Parliament. If a State Government is also a member, it must present the report in the State Legislature.
points: The Central Government must prepare an annual report on the working and affairs of the company.
This report must be prepared within three months of the annual general meeting where the audit report and CAG comments were placed.
The Central Government must lay this annual report, along with the audit report and CAG comments, before both Houses of Parliament.
If a State Government is also a member of the company, it must lay a copy of the prepared annual report before its State Legislature along with the audit report and CAG comments.
example: Asha Solar Power Private Limited is a Government company where both the Central Government and the State Government of Maharashtra are members. After the company holds its annual general meeting and reviews the audit report and comments from the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, the Central Government prepares an annual report within three months. Once ready, the Central Government lays this report, along with the audit report and CAG comments, before both Houses of Parliament. Following this, the Government of Maharashtra also takes a copy of this annual report and lays it before the State Legislature of Maharashtra together with the audit report and CAG comments.

terms.meaning: An official authority who checks government accounts and prepares audit reports.
A yearly gathering of company members to discuss business matters.
Presented officially to a governing body like Parliament or a State Legislature.

watch: Make sure to note that the three-month deadline applies to preparing the report after the annual general meeting, not to holding the meeting itself.
